cards.title: The Search for Investment Truth
cards.html:
In 1990, Ray Dalio asked a deceptively simple question: Can we build a portfolio that makes money consistently in all economic environments?

He called it the "Holy Grail of Investing" – not because it promised the highest returns, but because it promised something far more valuable: consistency without catastrophic failure.

The answer wasn't magical. It was mathematical. Dalio discovered that if you could find 10-15 truly uncorrelated return streams, you could reduce risk by 80% without sacrificing returns.

But here's the part most investors miss:

The Holy Grail isn't just about diversification. It's about finding the single best idea in each category and combining them with surgical precision.

Today, we're going to show you exactly that: one extraordinary equity engine, surrounded by 10-15 ultra-efficient return streams, all implemented with institutional-grade precision and priced in basis points, not percentages.

cards.title: The Simplicity Principle
cards.html:
Simplicity is the signature of truth.

Steve Jobs understood this deeply. When he returned to Apple in 1997, the company sold dozens of confusing products. His first move? Cut the product line to four computers. Just four.

The same principle applies to investing. The most sophisticated investors in the world – the SWFs managing trillions, the endowments compounding for centuries – they don't chase complexity. They pursue elegant simplicity backed by rigorous mathematics.

This presentation is designed for the smartest 1,024 humans in 2025 and their capital allocation teams at ADIA, Mubadala, Norway's Government Pension Fund, and the world's largest family offices. You deserve a strategy that respects your intelligence while honoring the principle that truth doesn't require ornamentation.

cards.title: The King of Kings Metric
cards.html:
Why Absolute Free Cash Flow Growth Dominates Everything

In 50 years of studying capital markets, one metric stands alone as the ultimate predictor of long-term wealth creation: absolute free cash flow growth.

Not revenue growth. Not earnings growth. Not EBITDA or any acronym invented by investment bankers to make mediocre businesses look attractive.

Free cash flow is the only number that cannot be manipulated by accounting tricks. It's the cash a business generates after paying all its bills, after reinvesting in growth, after maintaining its competitive position.

It's truth in numerical form.

Why "Absolute" Matters

We don't care about FCF margins. We care about absolute dollar growth.

A company growing FCF from $10B to $15B annually – adding $5 billion in real cash – creates more investable wealth than a small company improving margins from 20% to 25%.

Scale compounds. Percentages don't.

cards.title: Why Direct Ownership Changes Everything
cards.html:
The ETF Trap

Most "equity" portfolios own ETFs tracking indices. This creates three silent killers:

  1. Fee drag: 0.03-0.50% annually on every dollar
  2. Options impossibility: You can't write covered calls on SPY shares and capture premium
  3. Tax inefficiency: No individual name loss harvesting, forced capital gains distributions

Over 30 years, these three factors compound into a multi-million dollar wealth destruction for high-net-worth portfolios.

The Direct Ownership Advantage

Zero fee drag on your core equity engine. You own Apple shares directly, not through a fund charging fees to hold Apple for you.

Options income becomes possible – and systematic. Write covered calls when volatility spikes, sell cash-secured puts when markets panic.

Tax alpha through individual name harvesting. Sell Alphabet at a loss in a down year, buy Microsoft to maintain exposure, save six figures in taxes.

This alone justifies direct ownership for portfolios above $10 million.

cards.title: The Options Engine: Turning Volatility Into Income
cards.html:
Here's the secret the Absolute 27 unlocks: systematic options income without speculation.

We don't "trade" options. We run a rules-based engine that exploits two mathematical certainties:

1. Mean Reversion in Volatility

When great companies spike on euphoria (RSI > 70, trading 2+ standard deviations above the mean), implied volatility expands. Option premiums become expensive.

We sell covered calls at 5-10% out-of-the-money strikes, collecting 1-3% premiums for 30-45 days of exposure.

2. Panic Creates Opportunity

When markets crash and great companies sell off (RSI < 30, trading 2+ standard deviations below the mean), we want to own more.

We sell cash-secured puts at strikes where we'd happily buy shares, collecting premium while waiting for assignment.

cards.title: The Options Protocol: Systematic, Not Speculative
cards.html:
Trigger Conditions

RSI(14) crosses 70 (calls) or 30 (puts), stock moves 2+ standard deviations, implied volatility rank > 50th percentile, no earnings within 14 days

Strike Selection

5-10% out-of-the-money, preferring round numbers ($100, $150, $200) for maximum liquidity

Expiration Window

30-45 days to expiration (DTE) – the "theta sweet spot" where time decay accelerates

Position Sizing

Never more than 50% of a holding per cycle, maximum 25-35% total portfolio options exposure

Roll Rules

Close at 50% profit or 21 DTE, roll up/out if breached, stand down during earnings

These rules remove emotion. The system runs itself, generating 15-25% annual income on the equity sleeve – on top of the 12-18% organic business growth.

cards.title: Vehicle Selection: The Basis Point Battle
cards.html:
Every basis point of fee drag compounds against you for decades. On a $100 million portfolio, a 0.50% fee costs $500,000 annually – $15 million over 30 years before compounding.

We treat vehicle selection with the same rigor we apply to security selection. Every holding must pass our five-factor scorecard:

Expense Ratio (40% weight)

Target: Sub-5 basis points for core holdings. Acceptable: Up to 20 bps for specialized exposures. Avoid: Anything above 50 bps without extraordinary justification.

Liquidity (20% weight)

Average daily volume above $100M minimum. Prefer $500M+ for seamless execution at scale. Tight bid-ask spreads (< 0.05%) for institutional-size trades.

Tracking Error (15% weight)

Below 0.50% annually for index-tracking vehicles. We want pure beta, not active management hidden in a passive wrapper.

Tax Efficiency (15% weight)

ETF structure strongly preferred (in-kind redemption mechanism). Mutual funds acceptable only in tax-advantaged accounts. Avoid K-1 issuers for taxable portfolios.

Platform Access (10% weight)

Available on all major custodians (Schwab, Fidelity, Interactive Brokers, prime brokers). No proprietary vehicles requiring special accounts.

cards.title: Tax Location: The Hidden Alpha Source
cards.html:
Sophisticated investors don't just choose the right assets. They choose the right account for each asset.

The US tax code is extraordinarily complex, but it creates massive alpha opportunities for those who understand asset location. The basic principle:

"Put tax-inefficient assets in tax-advantaged accounts. Put tax-efficient assets in taxable accounts where they can compound with minimal drag."

For a $50 million portfolio, proper tax location can add 0.50-1.00% annual alpha – $25-50 million in cumulative wealth over three decades.

The basic principle: "Put tax-inefficient assets in tax-advantaged accounts. Put tax-efficient assets in taxable accounts where they can compound with minimal drag." For a $50 million portfolio, proper tax location can add 0.50-1.00% annual alpha – $25-50 million in cumulative wealth over three decades.

cards.title: Monthly Operations: Rebalancing & Reporting
cards.html:
Rebalancing Review

Each month, we compare actual allocations to target allocations. If any return stream has drifted more than 3 percentage points from target, we flag it for rebalancing.

Example: Target 38% equity in Balanced profile, currently 41% due to strong equity performance. Flag for 3% trim, redirect proceeds to underweight streams (likely bonds or managed futures).

Rebalancing is tactical, not mechanical. We consider:

  • Tax consequences of selling winners
  • Trading costs for small adjustments
  • Market conditions (avoid rebalancing into panics)

Monthly Reporting Package

Each client receives:

  • Performance Summary: Total return, return by sleeve, benchmark comparisons
  • Risk Metrics: Volatility, Sharpe ratio, max drawdown, rolling correlations
  • Fee Drag Update: Weighted average expense ratio across all holdings
  • Options Activity: Premiums collected, positions opened/closed, outstanding notional
  • Tax-Loss Harvest Log: Realized losses captured for tax efficiency

Institutional clients receive additional attribution analysis breaking down return sources.

No discretion. No guessing. Just mathematics and discipline.

cards.title: Risk Disclosure: What Can Go Wrong
cards.html:
Every investment strategy carries risks. Transparency demands we discuss them openly:

Equity Concentration Risk

27 names is concentrated vs. 500-stock indices. If several Tier 1 companies underperform simultaneously, portfolio returns suffer. Mitigation: Choose only the highest-quality FCF growers with durable moats.

Options Assignment Risk

Covered calls may be assigned, forcing sale of appreciated shares. Cash-secured puts may be assigned, requiring purchase at higher-than-market prices. Mitigation: Rules-based system limits exposure, accepts assignments as part of strategy.

Interest Rate Risk

Rising rates hurt bond values. TIPS, aggregate bonds, and REITs all correlate negatively with rate increases. Mitigation: Short-duration bias, diversification across asset classes.

Inflation Risk

Unexpected inflation erodes purchasing power. While TIPS, commodities, and gold provide protection, severe stagflation (1970s-style) challenges all portfolios. Mitigation: Real asset allocation (20-30% of portfolio).

Geopolitical Risk

Global companies face regulatory, currency, and political risks. Aramco specifically carries Middle East geopolitical risk. Mitigation: Geographic diversification, flexibility to substitute exposures.

cards.title: Frequently Asked Questions
cards.html:
Q: Can I add/remove names from the Absolute 27?

A: For portfolios $50M+, yes, with IC approval. Below $50M, customization dilutes benefits of systematic approach.

Q: What happens if I need liquidity?

A: Equity positions liquid daily. ETFs liquid daily. We can raise cash within 24-48 hours. Recommend maintaining 5-10% in T-Bills for unexpected needs.

Q: Do you offer ESG/impact versions?

A: We can screen out specific sectors (tobacco, weapons, fossil fuels) but this reduces return potential. Better approach: Earn maximum returns, donate to causes you care about.

Q: How do you handle currency risk for non-US clients?

A: We can add currency hedges via futures for portfolios $50M+. Below that, currency risk is accepted as part of global diversification.

Q: What if one of the Absolute 27 has a scandal/bankruptcy?

A: Immediate IC meeting. Sell position if fundamental thesis broken. Replace with next-highest FCF growth name. This has never happened in 10+ years because we choose only the highest-quality businesses.

Q: Can I see historical performance?

A: Yes, upon signing NDA. We provide full track record including 2020 COVID crash, 2022 bear market, detailed attribution analysis.
